001package io.jstach.rainbowgum.rolling;
002
003import java.io.File;
004import java.net.URI;
005import java.nio.file.Path;
006import java.util.function.Consumer;
007import java.util.function.Supplier;
008
009import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
010
011import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogConfig;
012import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogMetrics;
013import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogProperties;
014import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogProvider;
015import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogProviderRef;
016import io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation.LogConfigurable;
017import io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation.LogConfigurable.ConvertParameter;
018import io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation.LogConfigurable.DefaultParameter;
019import io.jstach.rainbowgum.file.DataSize;
020import io.jstach.rainbowgum.file.FileOutput;
021import io.jstach.rainbowgum.file.FileOutputBuilder;
022
023/**
024 * A {@link FileOutput} that rolls (renames the active file to a numbered archive and
025 * starts a fresh one) once it grows past {@code maxFileSize}, retaining at most
026 * {@code maxHistory} archives.
027 * <p>
028 * Deliberately size (not calendar/date) triggered and only supports a <code>%i</code>
029 * (rotation index) token in {@link #DEFAULT_FILE_NAME_PATTERN} - see
030 * {@code doc/overview.html}'s "Rolling Files" section for why: reopen-on-external-signal
031 * (e.g. via <code>logrotate</code>) remains the recommended approach for anything beyond
032 * "keep a small/desktop app from filling its disk", and that simpler need does not
033 * benefit from Logback-style calendar based archive naming.
034 * <p>
035 * Registered under the {@value #ROLLING_SCHEME} URI scheme (see
036 * {@code RollingConfigurator}), e.g. {@code rolling:///var/log/app.log?maxFileSize=...}.
037 * As with file URIs, a path starting with <code>/./</code>, as in
038 * {@code rolling:///./logs/app.log}, is relative to the working directory. Its properties
039 * are <code>logging.appender.{name}.output.rolling.</code> followed by a
040 * {@link RollingFileOutputBuilder} property name. {@code fileName}, {@code append},
041 * {@code prudent} and {@code bufferSize} mean the same as for {@link FileOutput} and are
042 * passed to the underlying file output this wraps. The {@code append} setting applies
043 * when the output is first opened. Replacement outputs always append so recovery
044 * preserves any active contents left behind by a failed rotation.
045 * <p>
046 * Failed automatic rotation attempts record {@link LogMetrics#ROLL_FAIL_METRIC} and an
047 * error alert identifying the active file. The event that triggered the failed rotation
048 * is not retried and also counts toward {@link LogMetrics#EVENTS_FAILED_METRIC}. The next
049 * write attempts to recover the output. Archive changes already completed before a
050 * failure are not rolled back. An explicit {@link #reopen()} after external rotation
051 * instead uses {@link LogMetrics#REOPEN_FAIL_METRIC}.
052 * <p>
053 * Only one process should rotate these files. Prudent mode locks individual writes, but
054 * does not coordinate archive rotation between processes.
055 */
056public interface RollingFileOutput extends FileOutput {
057
058        /**
059         * URI scheme for rolling file outputs.
060         */
061        static final String ROLLING_SCHEME = "rolling";
062
063        /**
064         * Default buffer size, the same as {@link FileOutput#DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE}.
065         */
066        static final DataSize DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE = FileOutput.DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE;
067
068        /**
069         * Default max file size before a roll is triggered: 10MB, matching Logback and Spring
070         * Boot's own default.
071         */
072        static final DataSize DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE = DataSize.ofMegabytes(10);
073
074        /**
075         * Default number of archives to retain - 7, matching Logback/Spring Boot's own
076         * default.
077         */
078        static final int DEFAULT_MAX_HISTORY = 7;
079
080        /**
081         * Default total archive size cap. {@link DataSize#ZERO} means unlimited.
082         */
083        static final DataSize DEFAULT_TOTAL_SIZE_CAP = DataSize.ZERO;
084
085        /**
086         * Default for whether archive pruning ({@code maxHistory}/{@code totalSizeCap}) also
087         * runs once at {@link #start(LogConfig)}, not just after each roll.
088         */
089        static final boolean DEFAULT_CLEAN_HISTORY_ON_START = false;
090
091        /**
092         * Default {@code fileNamePattern} - the literal text appended directly after the
093         * active file's own path (unlike Logback, never containing the base file name itself)
094         * with <code>%i</code> substituted for the rotation index, e.g. <code>app.log</code>
095         * with this pattern archives to <code>app.log.1</code>, <code>app.log.2</code>, etc.
096         * A pattern ending in <code>.gz</code> gzip compresses archives on rotation.
097         */
098        static final String DEFAULT_FILE_NAME_PATTERN = ".%i";
099
100        /**
101         * Creates a rolling file output provider from a URI reference - the entry point used
102         * by the {@value #ROLLING_SCHEME} scheme registration.
103         * @param ref uri reference, may have a query string of builder properties (same
104         * convention as {@link FileOutput#of(LogProviderRef)}).
105         * @return provider.
106         */
107        public static LogProvider<io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogOutput> of(LogProviderRef ref) {
108                return (name, config) -> provide(ref, name, config);
109        }
110
111        /**
112         * Creates a rolling file output provider from a lambda builder and uses the config
113         * properties from the returned log provider - mirrors
114         * {@link FileOutput#of(Consumer)}.
115         * @param consumer builder lambda.
116         * @return provider.
117         */
118        public static LogProvider<RollingFileOutput> of(Consumer<RollingFileOutputBuilder> consumer) {
119                return (name, config) -> {
120                        var builder = new RollingFileOutputBuilder(name);
121                        consumer.accept(builder);
122                        builder.fromProperties(config.properties());
123                        return builder.build().provide(name, config);
124                };
125        }
126
127        private static FileOutput provide(LogProviderRef ref, String name, LogConfig config) {
128                var b = new RollingFileOutputBuilder(name);
129                var uri = ref.uri();
130                var properties = config.properties();
131                LogProperties combined;
132                if (uri.getQuery() != null) {
133                        combined = LogProperties.of(uri, b.propertyPrefix(), properties, ref.keyOrNull());
134                        String s = uri.toString();
135                        int index = s.indexOf('?');
136                        uri = URI.create(s.substring(0, index));
137                }
138                else {
139                        combined = properties;
140                }
141                b.uri(uri);
142                b.fromProperties(combined);
143                return b.build().provide(name, config);
144        }
145
146        /**
147         * Creates a rolling file output provider.
148         * @param name name of output, not file name.
149         * @param uri file uri, set by the appender from its <code>output.uri</code>.
150         * @param fileName path of the active file, relative to the working directory unless
151         * absolute. Takes precedence over the uri.
152         * @param append whether or not to append to an existing file when first opened.
153         * @param prudent logback prudent mode where files are locked on each write.
154         * @param bufferSize buffer size, in
155         * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.file.DataSize#parse(String)} format when set by
156         * property, e.g. {@code 8KB}. Zero means unbuffered.
157         * @param maxFileSize max file size before a roll is triggered, in
158         * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.file.DataSize#parse(String)} format when set by
159         * property, e.g. {@code 10MB}.
160         * @param maxHistory number of archives to retain.
161         * @param totalSizeCap total archive size cap; zero means unlimited.
162         * @param cleanHistoryOnStart whether pruning also runs once at start, not just after
163         * each roll.
164         * @param fileNamePattern text appended to the active file's path to name each
165         * archive, see {@link RollingFileOutput#DEFAULT_FILE_NAME_PATTERN}; must contain
166         * <code>%i</code> and must not contain <code>%d</code> (date based rotation is not
167         * supported).
168         * @return rolling file output provider.
169         */
170        @LogConfigurable(name = "RollingFileOutputBuilder", prefix = LogProperties.OUTPUT_PREFIX + "rolling.")
171        public static LogProvider<RollingFileOutput> of(@LogConfigurable.KeyParameter String name,
172                        @LogConfigurable.PassThroughParameter @Nullable URI uri, @Nullable String fileName,
173                        @Nullable Boolean append, @Nullable Boolean prudent,
174                        @ConvertParameter("parseDataSize") @DefaultParameter("DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE") DataSize bufferSize,
175                        @ConvertParameter("parseDataSize") @DefaultParameter("DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE") DataSize maxFileSize,
176                        @DefaultParameter("DEFAULT_MAX_HISTORY") Integer maxHistory,
177                        @ConvertParameter("parseDataSize") @DefaultParameter("DEFAULT_TOTAL_SIZE_CAP") DataSize totalSizeCap,
178                        @DefaultParameter("DEFAULT_CLEAN_HISTORY_ON_START") Boolean cleanHistoryOnStart,
179                        @DefaultParameter("DEFAULT_FILE_NAME_PATTERN") String fileNamePattern) {
180                var parsedPattern = RollingPolicy.ParsedPattern.parse(fileNamePattern);
181                File file;
182                if (fileName != null) {
183                        file = new File(fileName);
184                }
185                else if (uri != null) {
186                        file = fileOf(uri);
187                }
188                else {
189                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("fileName and uri cannot both be unset.");
190                }
191                Path activeFile = file.toPath().toAbsolutePath();
192                String fileNameForDelegate = file.getPath();
193                long maxFileSize_ = maxFileSize.toBytes();
194                int maxHistory_ = maxHistory;
195                long totalSizeCap_ = totalSizeCap.toBytes();
196                boolean cleanHistoryOnStart_ = cleanHistoryOnStart;
197                return (n, config) -> {
198                        var fileBuilder = new FileOutputBuilder(n).fileName(fileNameForDelegate)
199                                .append(append == null ? true : append)
200                                .prudent(prudent)
201                                .bufferSize(bufferSize);
202                        var initialOutput = fileBuilder.build().provide(n, config);
203                        // append=false applies only to initial opening. Recovery must preserve any
204                        // active contents left behind by a failed rotation.
205                        var replacementProvider = fileBuilder.append(true).build();
206                        Supplier<FileOutput> supplier = () -> replacementProvider.provide(n, config);
207                        return new DefaultRollingFileOutput(activeFile, parsedPattern, maxFileSize_, maxHistory_, totalSizeCap_,
208                                        cleanHistoryOnStart_, supplier, initialOutput, config);
209                };
210        }
211
212        /**
213         * Converts a {@code maxFileSize} or {@code totalSizeCap} property value.
214         * @param value property value.
215         * @return data size.
216         * @see DataSize#parse(String)
217         */
218        static DataSize parseDataSize(String value) {
219                return DataSize.parse(value);
220        }
221
222        /*
223         * As with file URIs, a path starting with /./ is relative to the working directory.
224         */
225        private static File fileOf(URI uri) {
226                String rawPath = uri.getRawPath();
227                if (rawPath == null || rawPath.isEmpty() || rawPath.equals("/")) {
228                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Rolling file URI has no file path. Use rolling:///var/log/app.log, "
229                                        + "rolling:///./app.log for a file in the working directory, or the fileName property.");
230                }
231                if (rawPath.startsWith("/./")) {
232                        return Path.of(uri.getPath().substring(1)).toFile();
233                }
234                /* Through a file URI, since the decoded path on Windows is /C:/... */
235                return Path.of(URI.create("file://" + rawPath)).toFile();
236        }
237
238}
